Personal Relationship With Jesus
PUR-suh-nul ree-LAY-shun-ship with JEE-zus
phrase (noun)
A twentieth-century evangelical formula contrasting living faith with mere religion or churchgoing ('it's not a religion, it's a relationship'). The phrase rightly reaches for the personal knowing of God in Christ, but its individualistic packaging — 'personal,' 'me-and-Jesus' — often drops the lordship, the covenant, and the church that Scripture binds inseparably to that knowing.

Biblical Verdict

🟠
Examine
A true kernel — union with Christ and the knowing of God — shrunk to therapeutic individualism; recover the lordship, covenant, and church it drops.

Biblical Definition

There is a true and precious kernel here, for eternal life is indeed a knowing of a Person: 'this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent' (John 17:3). Believers are united to Christ — 'I am the vine, ye are the branches' (John 15:5) — and the Lord knows His own by name (John 10:14, 27). But Scripture's knowing of Christ is never the therapeutic, privatized 'relationship' of modern usage. It is covenantal: the believer is bound to Christ as a wife to a husband (Eph. 5:31-32), a member to a body (1 Cor. 12:27), a living stone in a temple (1 Pet. 2:5). It is submissive: to know Christ is to own Him as Lord — 'why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?' (Luke 6:46). And it is corporate: Christ loved and gave Himself for 'the church' (Eph. 5:25), and the Christian knows Him together with all saints (Eph. 3:18-19), not as a solitary soul. Union with Christ, knowing God, lordship, covenant, and the church are one cloth; the phrase keeps a true thread and too often unravels the rest.

Era

A true kernel — union with Christ and the knowing of God (John 17:3) — reduced to therapeutic individualism that drops lordship, covenant, and the church; recover the whole.

PERSONAL RELATIONSHIP WITH JESUS, phrase. A twentieth-century evangelical formula for living faith over against mere religion.

True kernel: eternal life is to know God in Christ (John 17:3); the believer is united to Christ (John 15:5) and known by Him (John 10:14).

Reduction: 'personal' is read as private and therapeutic — a me-and-Jesus intimacy detached from His lordship.

What it drops: covenant (Eph. 5:31-32), the church (Eph. 5:25), and submission to Christ as Lord (Luke 6:46) — recover the whole.

Key Scripture

John 17:3 — "And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent."

John 15:5 — "I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing."

Luke 6:46 — "And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?"

Ephesians 5:25 — "Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;"

1 Corinthians 12:27 — "Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular."

Philippians 3:8 — "Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ,"

Modern Corruption

A real truth — union with Christ and the knowing of God — is shrunk to a private, therapeutic intimacy that quietly drops the lordship, the covenant, and the church Scripture binds to it.

expand to see more

The corruption is not in affirming a personal knowing of Christ — Scripture affirms it richly — but in letting 'personal' collapse into 'private,' so that the bond with Jesus is severed from everything Scripture welds to it. In much modern usage 'a personal relationship with Jesus' means a warm, individual, inward intimacy — me and Jesus — with little reference to His authority over my life, the covenant that binds me, or the body to which He has joined me. Christ becomes a personal companion or therapist rather than the crucified and risen Lord. But Paul's knowledge of Christ was knowledge of 'Christ Jesus my Lord' (Phil. 3:8), and Jesus Himself rebuked the man who claims relationship without obedience: 'why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?' (Luke 6:46).

The reduction also privatizes what Scripture makes corporate. Christ did not give Himself for isolated individuals only but for 'the church' (Eph. 5:25); the believer is 'the body of Christ, and members in particular' (1 Cor. 12:27), able to comprehend Christ's love only 'with all saints' (Eph. 3:18). The me-and-Jesus framing, taken alone, lets a soul imagine it can have Christ while forsaking His people, His ordinances, and His ordained worship — exactly the self-chosen, church-less 'spirituality' the New Testament knows nothing of. To have the Head is to be joined to the body; one cannot embrace Christ and refuse the church He bought with His blood.

The recovery is to keep the kernel and restore the whole cloth. Yes — know Christ personally, intimately, savingly; eternal life is precisely this knowing (John 17:3), and the believer truly abides in Him as a branch in the vine (John 15:5). But that knowing is covenantal (the marriage of Christ and His church, Eph. 5:31-32), submissive (He is Lord, and to know Him is to obey Him), and corporate (known with all saints, in His body, under His ordinances). A 'personal relationship with Jesus' that drops His lordship is sentiment, not salvation; one that drops His church is a contradiction. Recover Christ as Savior, Lord, Husband, and Head, and the personal knowing becomes what it was always meant to be.

Hebrew Roots

A true kernel (union with Christ, knowing God, John 17:3) reduced to a private intimacy that drops lordship, covenant, and the church; Scripture welds them as one cloth — recover the whole.

expand to see more

English: a twentieth-century evangelical formula ('not a religion, a relationship'); the true kernel is the personal knowing of God in Christ.

The kernel: John 17:3 (eternal life is to know God) and John 15:5 (union with Christ as branch to vine).

What it must keep: lordship (Luke 6:46), covenant (Eph. 5:31-32), and the church (Eph. 5:25) — the threads the reduction drops.

Usage

"He boasted of a 'personal relationship with Jesus' while forsaking the assembling of the saints, as though one could keep the Head and cut off the body."

"Paul knew 'Christ Jesus my Lord' (Phil. 3:8); strip the lordship from the relationship and you have sentiment, not salvation."

"Know Christ intimately — but covenantally, submissively, and with all saints, for He gave Himself for the church, not for solitary souls."
